topics.label: Introduction to the complement lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing complement's importance and the challenges of its nomenclature.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic framework for understanding complement as a protein-cleavage cascade centered on C3 activation.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and the local activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pathogen recognition generates enough surface-bound C3b to cross the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement promotes pathogen elimination.

topics.label: Complement regulation and host-cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activity to prevent damage to host cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in particular complement components to their distinct clinical presentations.

topics.label: Pathogen complement evasion and protein A applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how pathogens circumvent complement, culminating in the practical use of an antibody-binding evasion protein.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture series and identifies adaptive immunity as the subject of the next lecture.
